CORPORATE OVERVIEW
UGI Corporation is a holding company that, through subsidiaries and affiliates, distributes, stores, transports and markets energy products and related services. In the U.S., we own and operate (1) natural gas and electric distribution utilities, (2) energy marketing (including RNG), midstream infrastructure, storage, natural gas gathering and processing, natural gas production and energy services businesses, and (3) a retail propane marketing and distribution business. In Europe, we market and distribute propane and other LPG, and market other energy products and services. Our subsidiaries and affiliates operate principally in the following four business segments:
• Utilities
• Midstream & Marketing
• UGI International
• AmeriGas Propane
The Utilities segment consists of the regulated natural gas (PA Gas Utility) and electric (Electric Utility) distribution businesses of our wholly owned subsidiary, UGI Utilities, and the regulated natural gas distribution business of our indirect, wholly owned subsidiary, Mountaineer. PA Gas Utility serves customers in eastern and central Pennsylvania and in portions of one Maryland county, and Mountaineer serves customers in West Virginia. Electric Utility serves customers in portions of Luzerne and Wyoming counties in northeastern Pennsylvania. PA Gas Utility is subject to regulation by the PAPUC and FERC and, with respect to its customers in Maryland, the MDPSC. Mountaineer is subject to regulation by the WVPSC and FERC. Electric Utility is subject to regulation by the PAPUC and FERC. During Fiscal 2026, we announced that UGI Utilities entered into a definitive agreement to divest its Electric Utility. The transaction includes the sale of approximately 2,700 miles of transmission and distribution lines and 14 substations in Pennsylvania’s Luzerne and Wyoming counties.
The Midstream & Marketing segment consists of energy-related businesses conducted by our indirect, wholly owned subsidiary, Energy Services. These businesses (i) conduct energy marketing, including RNG, in the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States, (ii) own and operate natural gas liquefaction, storage and vaporization facilities and propane-air mixing assets, (iii) manage natural gas pipeline and storage contracts, (iv) develop, own and operate pipelines, gathering infrastructure and gas storage facilities in the Marcellus and Utica Shale regions of Pennsylvania, eastern Ohio, and the panhandle of West Virginia, and (v) develop, own and operate RNG production facilities. Energy Services and its subsidiaries’ storage, LNG and portions of its midstream transmission operations are subject to regulation by FERC.
The UGI International segment consists of LPG distribution businesses conducted by our subsidiaries and affiliates in Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. Based on reported market volumes for 2025, which is the most recent information available, UGI International believes that it is the largest distributor of LPG in France, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg and Finland and one of the largest distributors of LPG in Norway, the Netherlands, Sweden and the United Kingdom. During Fiscal 2026, as part of our ongoing global LPG business portfolio optimization efforts, we completed the divestitures of our LPG distribution businesses in Austria, Romania, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. We also completed the divestiture of our cylinder business in the United Kingdom.
The AmeriGas Propane segment consists of the propane distribution business of AmeriGas Partners, an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of UGI. The Partnership conducts its domestic propane distribution business through its principal operating subsidiary, AmeriGas OLP, and is the nation’s largest retail propane distributor based on the volume of propane gallons distributed annually. The general partner of AmeriGas Partners is our wholly owned subsidiary, AmeriGas Propane, Inc.

Business Strategy
Our business strategy is to grow the Company by leveraging our core competencies of distributing, storing, transporting and marketing energy products, along with our extensive asset base, international experience, and access to customers, to drive organic growth in our existing businesses and in related and complementary businesses. We strive to be the preferred provider in all markets we serve and to return value to our shareholders.
In Fiscal 2026, we focused on enhancing our operations and financial profile to unlock greater shareholder value, including by optimizing our operating model, reinforcing a culture of high performance, and pursuing operational excellence. Specifically, we continue to focus on (1) driving reliable earnings growth, primarily through strong operational performance and investment in our regulated utilities; (2) executing operational improvements at AmeriGas Propane; (3) optimizing our portfolio; and (4) enhancing our capital structure and credit metrics to provide greater financial flexibility. Building on these efforts, on November 18, 2026, we announced the Separation. Following the Separation, UGI expects to be a natural gas infrastructure platform focused on its regulated natural gas utilities and complementary assets. For additional information regarding the Separation, see “Recent Events.”
On November 18, 2026, the Company announced that its Board of Directors unanimously approved a plan to separate the Company’s Global LPG business, comprising UGI International and AmeriGas Propane, into an independent, publicly traded company. The Separation is intended to be tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Following the Separation, the Company will be a natural gas infrastructure company consisting of its regulated natural gas utilities, operated through UGI Utilities and Mountaineer, and the complementary assets of Energy Services.
The Separation is expected to be completed during the second half of calendar year 2027. Completion of the Separation is subject to, among other things, final approval from the Board of Directors, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 to be filed with the SEC, and satisfaction of other customary conditions, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under the Company’s and its subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements. There can be no assurance that any Separation will occur or, if it does occur, that it will be completed on the structure, terms, or timing currently contemplated, or that it will qualify as tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
ESG Strategy
At UGI, we are committed to advancing a sustainable future by equipping communities and customers with safe, affordable, and reliable energy solutions while creating long-term value through responsible stewardship of our operations, people, and the environment.
The three pillars that comprise UGI’s environmental, social, and governance (“ESG”) approach are:
• Environmental Compliance & Stewardship : Meet regulatory requirements and industry benchmarks for GHG emissions reduction, energy efficiency, and environmental stewardship while proactively managing environmental performance across our operations.
• Social Responsibility : Enrich the lives of customers, communities, and employees through reliable service delivery, community partnerships, competitive employee programs and well-being initiatives.
• Governance Excellence : Maintain strong governance, risk management practices, transparent and consistent reporting, and ongoing stakeholder communication while integrating ESG considerations into strategic decision-making.
To support this strategy, we have made the following ESG-related commitments which have either been completed or remain on track for completion within the timeline stated:
• Scope 1 GHG Emissions Reduction Commitment – Reduce Scope 1 GHG emissions by 55% by 2025 (using Fiscal 2020 as a baseline). We exceeded this target, reducing Scope 1 GHG emissions by 62% as of Fiscal 2025.
• Methane Emissions Reduction Commitment – We remain on track to reduce methane emission by 92% reduction by 2030 (using Fiscal 2020 as a baseline), and 95% reduction by 2040 (using Fiscal 1999 as a baseline).
• Pipeline Replacement and Betterment Commitment – Replace all cast iron pipelines by 2027 and all bare steel by 2041. PA Gas Utility completed replacement of the cast iron portion of its mains during Fiscal 2026. These activities

Risks Relating to the Separation
The Separation may not be completed on the anticipated timeline, on the terms currently contemplated or at all, and, if completed, may not achieve the intended benefits. On November 18, 2026, we announced that our Board of Directors had unanimously approved the Separation that is intended to be tax-free to us and our shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. Following the Separation, the Company will be a natural gas infrastructure company consisting of its regulated natural gas utilities, operated through UGI Utilities and Mountaineer, and the complementary assets of Energy Services. We expect to complete the Separation during the second half of calendar year 2027. Completion of the Separation is subject to, among other things, final approval from the Board of Directors, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 to be filed with the SEC, and satisfaction of other customary conditions, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under our and our subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements. The Separation is complex, and unanticipated developments or changes, including changes in law, macroeconomic conditions, the credit and capital markets, or conditions in our industries or regulatory environment, or delays or conditions imposed in connection with required approvals or consents, could delay or prevent completion of the Separation or cause it to occur on terms or with a structure that is different from, or less favorable than, what we currently anticipate. There can be no assurance that the Separation will occur or, if one does occur, that it will be completed on the structure, terms, or timing currently contemplated, or that it will qualify as tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
Whether or not we complete the Separation, our ongoing businesses may face material challenges in connection with the Separation, including, but not limited to:
• the diversion of our management’s attention from operating and growing our business as a result of the significant amount of time and effort required to execute the Separation, including any related consultation processes with employee representatives;
• foreseen and unforeseen costs and expenses that will be incurred in connection with the Separation, including accounting, tax, legal and other professional services costs, and potential prepayment charges and write-offs of deferred costs related to establishing new capital structures;
• costs or inefficiencies associated with incremental costs related to the Separation, unanticipated delays in establishing infrastructure or processes for the new LPG Company, and costs and resources required to effectuate the Separation that may be significantly higher than what we currently anticipate;
• retaining existing business and operational relationships, including with customers and suppliers that may have rights to terminate their agreement as a result of the Separation, and with employees, as well as cultivating new business relationships; and
• potential negative reactions from the financial markets if we fail to complete the Separation in its currently intended form, within the anticipated time frame or at all.
Even if the Separation is completed, we may not realize some or all of the anticipated strategic, financial, operational or other benefits, or those benefits may be delayed. These include sharper strategic alignment, capital structures and capital return policies tailored to each company, greater capital and strategic flexibility, and the ability of investors to value each company based on its distinct operational and financial characteristics. If we do not complete the Separation, or do not realize its anticipated benefits, our business, financial condition, results of operations and the price of our Common Stock could be materially adversely affected.
If the Separation occurs, our financial and operational profile will change, and we will be a smaller, less diversified company than we are today. If the Separation occurs, it will result in two smaller, less diversified companies, each with a more concentrated area of focus. As a result, each company may be more vulnerable to changing market conditions, regulatory developments, weather, commodity price movements and competitive pressures, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. The diversification of revenues, costs and cash flows will diminish as a result of the Separation, such that each company’s ability to fund capital expenditures and investments, pay dividends and service its debt may be diminished. In Fiscal 2026, UGI International and AmeriGas Propane together contributed approximately 56% of our consolidated revenues and 36% of our consolidated earnings before interest expense and income taxes. The loss of these earnings and cash flows may lead rating agencies to downgrade our subsidiary credit ratings or place them on negative watch, increasing our borrowing costs and affecting our liquidity.
